subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does the actual Gateway request-dispatch path contain a reachable merge, assignment, or property-copy sink that turns parsed prototype-named keys into prototype mutation?
rationale: The report concerns a protected security boundary, but its proposed global reviver and disconnect behavior are broader than the demonstrated evidence and could alter valid extensible payload handling.

options.title: Validate the real sink first
options.body: Add a focused WebSocket regression probe and close as non-vulnerable if prototype state remains unchanged across representative core and plugin-dispatched requests.

options.title: Reject prototype keys defensively
options.body: Introduce a centralized parse-boundary rejection only if security owners intentionally want defense in depth despite no demonstrated mutation sink.

recommendation.title: Validate the real sink first
recommendation.body: Add a focused WebSocket regression probe and close as non-vulnerable if prototype state remains unchanged across representative core and plugin-dispatched requests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available history-based candidate for recent Gateway security-boundary review.
